# libraryquery

```go
import "dekart/src/server/dark/libraryquery"
```

Package libraryquery builds read\-only SQL for choosing rows of a catalogued table by area code, category and brand.

The package is pure: it takes a table description and a selection and returns SQL text. It reads no environment, clock, network or database and keeps no state, so the same input always gives the same text.

### Trust model

Identifiers \(schema, table and column names\) come from the caller's catalogue and are always double\-quoted, with embedded double quotes doubled. Selection values \(area code, category and brand ids\) come from untrusted input and are never quoted into SQL unless they match a strict pattern first:

- an area code is exactly 2, 4 or 7 ASCII digits;
- a category or brand id is 1 to 64 characters of ASCII lowercase letters, digits and underscore.

A value that does not match is rejected with [ErrInvalidArea](<#ErrInvalidIdentifier>) or [ErrInvalidID](<#ErrInvalidIdentifier>); it is never escaped and emitted. Accepted values are still written as single\-quoted literals with embedded single quotes doubled, as a second layer. No value is ever emitted as an identifier, and nothing in the output depends on the caller's locale.

### Category access

A table can carry a category column. The caller passes the set of category ids the reader may see; the emitted filter uses the intersection of that set and the requested categories, so a category that is not allowed can never reach the SQL. When the intersection is empty, building fails with [ErrNoAllowedCategory](<#ErrInvalidIdentifier>).

### Output shape

Every statement is a single SELECT of the table's columns with an optional WHERE clause of AND\-ed conditions in fixed order: area, category, brand. Lists inside IN \(...\) are sorted and deduplicated.

## Constants

<a name="MaxListSize"></a>

```go
const (
    // MaxListSize is the largest number of category or brand ids accepted in one list.
    MaxListSize = 500
    // MaxSampleLimit is the largest row limit [BuildSample] accepts.
    MaxSampleLimit = 1000
)
```

<a name="IDPattern"></a>IDPattern is the pattern a category or brand id must match: 1 to 64 ASCII lowercase letters, digits or underscores.

```go
const IDPattern = `^[a-z0-9_]{1,64}$`
```

## Variables

<a name="ErrInvalidIdentifier"></a>Errors returned by the builders. Compare with [errors.Is](<https://pkg.go.dev/errors/#Is>); the wrapped text adds the offending field name but never echoes the rejected value.

```go
var (
    // ErrInvalidIdentifier is returned for an empty, over-long or NUL-containing table or column name.
    ErrInvalidIdentifier = errors.New("libraryquery: invalid identifier")
    // ErrNoColumns is returned when a table lists no columns.
    ErrNoColumns = errors.New("libraryquery: table has no columns")
    // ErrInvalidArea is returned when an area code is not 2, 4 or 7 ASCII digits.
    ErrInvalidArea = errors.New("libraryquery: invalid area code")
    // ErrAreaLevelUnsupported is returned when the table has no column for the length of the area code.
    ErrAreaLevelUnsupported = errors.New("libraryquery: table cannot be filtered at this area level")
    // ErrInvalidID is returned when a category or brand id does not match [IDPattern].
    ErrInvalidID = errors.New("libraryquery: invalid id")
    // ErrCategoryRequired is returned when the table has a category column and no category was requested.
    ErrCategoryRequired = errors.New("libraryquery: at least one category is required")
    // ErrNoAllowedCategory is returned when none of the requested categories is in the allowed set.
    ErrNoAllowedCategory = errors.New("libraryquery: no requested category is allowed")
    // ErrCategoriesUnsupported is returned when categories are requested from a table without a category column.
    ErrCategoriesUnsupported = errors.New("libraryquery: table has no category column")
    // ErrBrandsUnsupported is returned when brands are requested from a table without a brand column.
    ErrBrandsUnsupported = errors.New("libraryquery: table has no brand column")
    // ErrTooManyValues is returned when a list holds more than [MaxListSize] entries.
    ErrTooManyValues = errors.New("libraryquery: too many values")
    // ErrInvalidLimit is returned for a sample limit outside 1 to [MaxSampleLimit].
    ErrInvalidLimit = errors.New("libraryquery: invalid limit")
)
```

<a name="Build"></a>
## func Build

```go
func Build(table Table, selection Selection, allowed []string) (string, error)
```

Build returns the SELECT statement that reads the rows of table matching selection.

allowed is the set of category ids the reader may see; it is only consulted when the table has a category column, where the emitted filter uses the intersection of allowed and selection.Categories.

Escaping: schema, table and column names are double\-quoted with embedded double quotes doubled; area, category and brand values must match their strict patterns first and are then emitted as single\-quoted literals with embedded single quotes doubled. A value that fails validation is rejected, never escaped. The result is one statement with no trailing semicolon.

Errors: [ErrNoColumns](<#ErrInvalidIdentifier>), [ErrInvalidIdentifier](<#ErrInvalidIdentifier>), [ErrInvalidArea](<#ErrInvalidIdentifier>), [ErrAreaLevelUnsupported](<#ErrInvalidIdentifier>), [ErrInvalidID](<#ErrInvalidIdentifier>), [ErrCategoryRequired](<#ErrInvalidIdentifier>), [ErrNoAllowedCategory](<#ErrInvalidIdentifier>), [ErrCategoriesUnsupported](<#ErrInvalidIdentifier>), [ErrBrandsUnsupported](<#ErrInvalidIdentifier>) and [ErrTooManyValues](<#ErrInvalidIdentifier>). Build never returns partial SQL together with an error.

<details><summary>Example</summary>
<p>

Build a query for two categories in one city, keeping only the categories the reader may see.

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"dekart/src/server/dark/libraryquery"
)

func main() {
	table := libraryquery.Table{
		Schema:         "lib",
		Name:           "places",
		Columns:        []string{"name", "lat", "lon"},
		AreaColumns:    []libraryquery.AreaColumn{{Length: 4, Column: "city_code"}},
		CategoryColumn: "category_id",
	}
	sql, err := libraryquery.Build(table, libraryquery.Selection{
		Area:       "3273",
		Categories: []string{"cafe", "bar", "pharmacy"},
	}, []string{"cafe", "pharmacy"})
	fmt.Println(sql)
	fmt.Println(err)
}
```

#### Output

```
SELECT "name", "lat", "lon"
FROM "lib"."places"
WHERE "city_code" = '3273'
  AND "category_id" IN ('cafe', 'pharmacy')
<nil>
```

</p>
</details>

<details><summary>Example (Hostile Identifier)</summary>
<p>

Identifiers are quoted with embedded double quotes doubled.

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"dekart/src/server/dark/libraryquery"
)

func main() {
	table := libraryquery.Table{Name: `places"; DROP TABLE places; --`, Columns: []string{`na"me`}}
	sql, err := libraryquery.Build(table, libraryquery.Selection{}, nil)
	fmt.Println(sql)
	fmt.Println(err)
}
```

#### Output

```
SELECT "na""me"
FROM "places""; DROP TABLE places; --"
<nil>
```

</p>
</details>

<details><summary>Example (Hostile Input)</summary>
<p>

Hostile values are rejected, not escaped: nothing is built from them.

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"dekart/src/server/dark/libraryquery"
)

func main() {
	table := libraryquery.Table{Name: "places", Columns: []string{"name"}, CategoryColumn: "category_id"}
	sql, err := libraryquery.Build(table, libraryquery.Selection{
		Categories: []string{"cafe' OR '1'='1"},
	}, []string{"cafe"})
	fmt.Printf("%q\n", sql)
	fmt.Println(err)
}
```

#### Output

```
""
libraryquery: invalid id: categories
```

</p>
</details>

<a name="BuildSample"></a>
## func BuildSample

```go
func BuildSample(table Table, selection Selection, allowed []string, limit int) (string, error)
```

BuildSample returns the statement of [Build](<#Build>) followed by a LIMIT clause of limit rows.

limit must be between 1 and [MaxSampleLimit](<#MaxListSize>); it is formatted as a decimal integer, never taken as text. All other escaping and errors are those of [Build](<#Build>), plus [ErrInvalidLimit](<#ErrInvalidIdentifier>).

<details><summary>Example</summary>
<p>

A sample is the same query with a row limit.

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"dekart/src/server/dark/libraryquery"
)

func main() {
	table := libraryquery.Table{Name: "roads", Columns: []string{"name"}}
	sql, _ := libraryquery.BuildSample(table, libraryquery.Selection{}, nil, 20)
	fmt.Println(sql)
}
```

#### Output

```
SELECT "name"
FROM "roads"
LIMIT 20
```

</p>
</details>

<a name="Intersect"></a>
## func Intersect

```go
func Intersect(requested, allowed []string) []string
```

Intersect returns the ids present in both lists, sorted and without duplicates. Ids that do not match [IDPattern](<#IDPattern>) are dropped, so the result is always safe to pass on. It does not modify its arguments.

<details><summary>Example</summary>
<p>

Intersect keeps ids present in both lists.

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"dekart/src/server/dark/libraryquery"
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println(libraryquery.Intersect([]string{"cafe", "bar", "cafe"}, []string{"bar", "bank"}))
}
```

#### Output

```
[bar]
```

</p>
</details>

<a name="ValidArea"></a>
## func ValidArea

```go
func ValidArea(code string) bool
```

ValidArea reports whether code is empty \(no area filter\) or exactly 2, 4 or 7 ASCII digits.

<details><summary>Example</summary>
<p>

Area codes are 2, 4 or 7 ASCII digits.

```go
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"dekart/src/server/dark/libraryquery"
)

func main() {
	fmt.Println(libraryquery.ValidArea("3273"), libraryquery.ValidArea("3273' OR 1=1"), libraryquery.ValidArea(""))
}
```

#### Output

```
true false true
```

</p>
</details>

<a name="AreaColumn"></a>
## type AreaColumn

AreaColumn names the column that holds area codes of one length.

```go
type AreaColumn struct {
    // Length is the number of digits of the area codes in Column: 2, 4 or 7.
    Length int
    // Column is the column name; it is quoted as an identifier.
    Column string
}
```

<a name="Selection"></a>
## type Selection

Selection is the untrusted part of a query: which area, categories and brands to keep.

```go
type Selection struct {
    // Area is an area code of 2, 4 or 7 ASCII digits, or empty for no area filter.
    Area string
    // Categories are the requested category ids. Required, at least one, when the table has a category column.
    Categories []string
    // Brands are optional brand ids, allowed only when the table has a brand column.
    Brands []string
}
```

<a name="Table"></a>
## type Table

Table describes a relation to read from. All names are identifiers: they are quoted, never validated against a pattern, so they must come from a trusted catalogue and not from a request.

```go
type Table struct {
    // Schema is the optional schema name.
    Schema string
    // Name is the table or view name.
    Name string
    // Columns are the columns to select, in order. At least one is required.
    Columns []string
    // AreaColumns lists the columns that area filters apply to, one per code length. Empty when the table has no area filter.
    AreaColumns []AreaColumn
    // CategoryColumn is the column holding category ids, or empty when rows have no category.
    CategoryColumn string
    // BrandColumn is the column holding brand ids, or empty when rows have no brand.
    BrandColumn string
}
```
